definition: Refine means to improve something through small, careful changes, especially by removing flaws or impurities.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word refine. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know refine should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: After dozens of attempts, the chef continued to refine his signature tomato sauce, adjusting one ingredient at a time until the flavor was exactly right.
To tweak something is to make one small, casual adjustment, while to refine it is to keep making careful improvements toward a polished result.
To refine something is to improve it noticeably, while to perfect it is to remove every last flaw until nothing could be better.

Polish means to improve something until it is smooth and finished — you polish an essay or a routine in its final stage. Refine covers the longer haul: a series of small, careful changes that remove flaws bit by bit. Polishing is the last pass; refining is the whole patient process.

Hone means to sharpen — literally an edge, and figuratively a skill perfected through repeated practice, like honing a jump shot. Refine applies more widely: recipes, designs, processes, and prose are refined through small, careful improvements. You hone what you practice; you refine what you keep improving.

Enhance means to raise something's quality or value by adding to it — better lighting enhances a room. Refine improves by adjusting and removing flaws, not by adding more. An enhanced version has something extra; a refined version is the same thing made more precise.

So began a season of refining.
Nothing was redesigned outright; nothing new was bolted on.
